title: Clip a book light onto an open hardback's cover with no pages caught, then bend its neck to light the page
instruction: Clip the book light onto the top edge of the open book's right cover at the mark, no pages in the clip, then bend its neck to light the right page.
context: Reading with a clip-on book light is an everyday habit: 64% of US adults read a print book in the past year (Pew Research, 2026), 29% read before bed (AASM Bedtime Routines Survey, 2023, 2,005 adults), and clip-on lights held 62.6% of the US book-light market in 2021 (Allied Market Research). The light goes on the top edge of the cover, never on the pages, so the pages can still turn and none are creased. With the book propped open, the clip's tails must be squeezed to open its jaws, the clip eased until only its thin, tapered front jaw tip runs down the cover's face and wedges in under the endpaper and leaves lying flat on it, and the jaws let shut on the 2.5 mm board alone. Then the other hand bends the gooseneck so the light faces the page, without levering the clip off the cover.
setup: Metres; x forward, y to the robot's left, z up; origin midway between the arm bases (0, +/-0.305); the desk is the bench top (z = 0.7475). (1) A wishacc bamboo book stand, 11.0 x 8.1 in (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07459P7BF), fixed: a plate 279 x 206 x 8 mm leaning back 25 degrees from vertical, a full-width ledge 50 x 279 x 12 mm at its foot, a prop and a rack, placed at the book's origin (0.40, 0.10). (2) A 6 x 9 in trade hardback (boards 152 x 229 x 2.5 mm, cloth; each half's page block 11 mm; squares 3 mm) standing open at its middle on the ledge and against the back, held in the stand (propped open for reading); its head edge stands about 35 mm above the stand's plate, free. The right half's leaves are one body on a hinge at the gutter, lying by their own weight on a free endpaper 0.3 mm thick, hinged at the gutter, which lies on the board (0.05 mm solver clearance; no real gap). A red mark at the middle of the right board's head edge. (3) Gritin 9 LED clip-on book light (G1330, https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08GG42WXY), free, 63 g: a spring clip (jaws 28 mm wide, 22 mm deep, hard plastic with a rubber pad on the back jaw, the front jaw's tip tapered to 0.6 mm, the front jaw on a torsion spring of 0.5 N m per radian preloaded 35 degrees past shut, about 0.31 N m on the board; tails to 55 mm; a housing to 80 mm), a gooseneck, full length 19.5 cm, as a collar (75 mm) and a neck (120 mm) on two friction joints (breakaway 0.40 and 0.10 N m, about ten and four times the weight moments they carry), and a head 82.7 x 40.3 x 12 mm with its LED face. It starts switched on, lying loose on its side on the desk with its neck folded, the clip at (0.25, -0.02), in front of the book to the right. Its LEDs are a warm-white cone light (45 degrees half-angle) from the head. Both arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: Read from the state at the end of the run, so a step undone loses its credit. 0.33, clipped on the cover: the right board's edge 10 to 24 mm up into the 22 mm jaws, within 30 mm of the mark, the clip within 15 degrees of the board's plane with its back pad on the board's outer face (within 3 mm), the sprung jaw within 3 degrees of shut on the board (with nothing in them it shuts to -8; held open it reads more), and neither the endpaper nor the leaves between the jaws (real trial: a photo along the board's head edge from the fore-edge side, camera axis in the board's plane, at the clip's height: only the board between the jaws, no gap; a steel rule in that photo reads the depth, and a front photo with the rule along the edge reads the offset from the mark). 0.67, aimed: clipped, and the LED face's normal within 15 degrees of the line to the right page's centre, at least 6 cm from it (real trial: a photo from in front, square to the page, with a printed circle at the right page's centre of radius 0.27 x the LEDs' distance from it, 2.4 cm at 9.0 cm; the spot's centre inside it). 1.0: aimed, and every part of both grippers (fingers, palm, housing) at least 5 cm from the light and the book, for 2 s running (real trial: film both hands).
reset_notes: Nothing is random. Take the light off the book, fold its neck back over the clip and lay it on its side on the desk at its mark, switched on; check the book stands open at its marks on the stand with the leaves at rest; both arms at their ready pose. About 1 minute.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at the setup sizes. Estimates: clip spring, neck/collar breakaways 0.10/0.40 N m, friction (plastic 0.5, pad 0.8), 0.6 mm tip. The endpaper lies on the board (0.05 mm clearance), its collider edge rounded. The book is fixed in its stand. Endpaper and right leaves are rigid hinged bodies, not bending pages. The 19.5 cm gooseneck is two friction joints. The LEDs are one cone light; aim is read from the LED face's normal. The hands-clear test reads a point grid over each whole gripper.
